review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Motion versus stopping/rest, displacement process versus vector quantity, velocity versus speed, angular quantities and measurements, intersecting motion types, mechanical oscillation and malformed braking entries.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. OpenStax physics chapters and Gramota support selected corrections. Definitions are paraphrased; translations, scope restrictions and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All additions use U1 and unspecified strength. Motion and rest use a fixed reference frame and time scope. A transition, a resulting state and a measured quantity remain distinct. Angular quantities are not linear quantities or revolution counts merely because their English names share velocity or acceleration.

sense_decisions.scope: The vector rate of position change. Split this meaning from the dictionary scalar-speed gloss.
The directed change between initial and final positions in one frame; not path length or the act of moving.
Rate and orientation of rotation, expressed with angular units per time. Distinct from linear velocity and rotations counted per time.
Rate of angular-velocity change. Keep separate from the existing linear acceleration quantity and from speeding up.
A unit for angular velocity, separate from a rotation-frequency unit.
The rad/s angular-velocity unit. Do not identify it with one revolution per second.
A unit for angular acceleration.
The rad/s2 angular-acceleration unit.
Measurement of the specified quantity, distinct from measurement of a similarly named scalar or frequency.
Measurement of the specified quantity, distinct from measurement of a similarly named scalar or frequency.
Measurement of the specified quantity, distinct from measurement of a similarly named scalar or frequency.
Measurement of the specified quantity, distinct from measurement of a similarly named scalar or frequency.
Motion along a straight line; speed need not be constant.
Motion along a circular path.
The scalar speed is constant over the selected interval; direction may change.
The scalar speed changes over the selected interval.
Straight-line motion with constant nonzero velocity in the chosen frame.
Circular motion at constant nonzero speed; the velocity direction changes.
Circular motion whose speed changes.
Motion that repeats its physical configuration at equal time intervals. Not every oscillation has exact periodicity.
Back-and-forth physical motion around an equilibrium or reference configuration. Restrict the broader oscillation process to mechanical motion.
The ideal undamped mechanical oscillation with sinusoidal displacement and a linear restoring response.
The harmonic mechanical model restricted to motion along one straight line.
An oscillatory motion with decreasing amplitude. Exclude overdamped or critically damped non-oscillatory returns to equilibrium.
The maximum absolute linear offset from the reference in an oscillation, or its time-varying envelope. This length sense excludes voltage and angular amplitudes.
The process of decreasing scalar motion speed. It need not reach rest; do not use the dictionary speeding-up genus.
The transition from rest to motion in a specified frame. Distinct from continued motion and from the resulting speed.
The very large movement branch still contains mixed generated verb senses; no blanket migration is made.
Rotational frequency counts turns per time and remains distinct from angular velocity.
Existing physical acceleration retains its direct genus and its Q12 measurement conditions.
Speed measurement is scalar; a speedometer is not automatically a full velocity-vector instrument.
Existing metre-per-second unit is reused; no unit/quantity identity is asserted.
Do not import the oscillation-as-wave genus or require all physical oscillations to be strictly periodic.
The dictionary brake verb gloss unnecessarily requires a full stop; the reviewed physical sense also includes slowing.
Rigid-body translation and generic relocation need different scopes; defer the former instead of importing a constant-speed restriction.

review.limits: No traffic advice, stopping distances, friction coefficients, force calculations or numerical device performance. No new blanket exclusions. Movement at constant scalar speed need not have a constant velocity vector. Braking entries select physical motion; figurative hindrance and physiological inhibition require separate senses. Translation, trajectory, inertia, momentum, mixed movement descendants and general amplitude dimensions remain queued. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Replace the cessation-as-motion genus and remove the motion/cessation contrary. Preserve the existing motion/rest contrary and all unrelated exclusion witnesses.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Existing motion, rest, relocation, rotation, oscillation, speed, acceleration and braking records are reused. Russian stem matches exposed generated braking records before a duplicate could be added.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
